questions.question: Which of the following is a neutralisation reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **neutralisation reaction** is a chemical reaction in which an **acid** and a **base** react quantitatively with each other to form **water** and a **salt**.
 
• The reaction **NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O** involves **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, which is a **strong base**, and **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, which is a **strong acid**. They react to produce **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, a neutral salt, and **water (H₂O)**. ***Hence, the statement representing this reaction is correct.***
 
• In the reaction **Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu**, **Iron (Fe)** displaces **Copper (Cu)** from the **Copper Sulphate** solution because iron is more reactive. This is a **single displacement reaction**, not neutralisation. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The reaction **CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂** represents the **thermal decomposition** of **Calcium Carbonate** into **Calcium Oxide** and **Carbon Dioxide** upon heating. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• In the reaction **Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂**, **Zinc (Zn)** reacts with **Hydrochloric Acid** to produce **Zinc Chloride** and **Hydrogen gas**. This is another example of a **displacement reaction**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Neutralisation:**
 
 
• Neutralisation reactions are generally **exothermic** in nature, meaning they release **heat energy** during the process.
 
• The **heat of neutralisation** is the change in **enthalpy** when one equivalent of an acid is neutralised by one equivalent of a base.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale and Indicators:**
 
 
• In a complete neutralisation of a strong acid and a strong base, the resulting solution has a **pH value** of **7** at **25 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Phenolphthalein** is a common **indicator** used in these reactions; it turns **pink** in basic solutions and becomes **colourless** when the solution is neutralised or acidic.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• **Antacids:** **Magnesium Hydroxide**, commonly known as **Milk of Magnesia**, is used to neutralise excess **hydrochloric acid** in the stomach to treat **acidity**.
 
• **Soil Treatment:** If the **soil** is too acidic, farmers add **Quick Lime (Calcium Oxide)** or **Slaked Lime (Calcium Hydroxide)** to neutralise it for better crop growth.
 
• **Insect Stings:** The effect of an **ant sting**, which contains **methanoic acid (formic acid)**, can be neutralised by rubbing **moist baking soda (Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate)** or **calamine solution**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Salts Formed:**
 
 
• A **strong acid** reacting with a **strong base** produces a **neutral salt** (e.g., **NaCl**).
 
• A **strong acid** reacting with a **weak base** produces an **acidic salt** (e.g., **Ammonium Chloride**).
 
• A **weak acid** reacting with a **strong base** produces a **basic salt** (e.g., **Sodium Acetate**).
 
 
 
• **Arrhenius Theory:** According to the **Arrhenius definition**, an **acid** provides **Hydrogen ions (H+)** and a **base** provides **Hydroxide ions (OH-)** in aqueous solutions. During neutralisation, these ions combine to form **water (H₂O)**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of liquids?

options.text: No fixed shape but fixed volume

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No fixed shape but fixed volume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Liquids** are a state of matter characterized by their ability to flow and take the **shape** of the container they occupy, which means they have **no fixed shape**. ***Hence, statement 3 is the correct characteristic.***

• Despite changing shape, a liquid maintains a **fixed volume** because its **particles** are close together and held by relatively strong **intermolecular forces** that prevent them from expanding to fill the entire space like a gas.

• The **particles** in a liquid have enough **kinetic energy** to move past one another, which accounts for the property of **fluidity**.

• Unlike **gases**, liquids are almost **incompressible** even under high **pressure** due to the minimal **intermolecular spaces** between the particles.

• When poured into a **container**, a liquid will fill the bottom part first and maintain a distinct **surface** level, unlike **solids** which retain their own shape or gases which occupy the entire volume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Solids:**

• Matter in the **solid state** has both a **fixed shape** and a **fixed volume**.

• The **particles** are packed tightly in a regular **lattice** structure and can only **vibrate** about their fixed positions.

• They have the highest **density** and strongest **intermolecular forces** compared to liquids and gases.

• **Gases:**

• Matter in the **gaseous state** has **no fixed shape** and **no fixed volume**.

• The **particles** are far apart and move in **random motion** at high speeds, filling any available space.

• Gases are highly **compressible** and have very low **density**.

• **Properties of Liquids:**

• **Viscosity:** This refers to the **resistance to flow**. For instance, **honey** is more viscous than **water**.

• **Surface Tension:** The cohesive forces between **molecules** at the surface of a liquid cause it to behave like a **stretched membrane**.

• **Boiling Point:** The **temperature** at which a liquid turns into a gas at a given **pressure**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Kinetic Molecular Theory:** This theory explains that the **physical state** of matter is determined by the balance between the **kinetic energy** of the particles and the **attractive forces** between them.

• **Diffusion:** This is the process where particles move from a **high concentration** to a **low concentration**. Diffusion occurs in liquids but is much slower than in **gases** due to the density of the particles.

• **Phase Change:** A liquid can change into a solid through **freezing** (loss of energy) or into a gas through **evaporation** or **boiling** (gain of energy).

• **Density:** Generally, the **density** of a substance in its liquid state is slightly lower than in its solid state, with the notable **anomaly** of **water**, which is most dense at **4°C**.

questions.question:
A ball is dropped from rest. What will be the velocity of the ball after falling 20 m?
(Take, g = 10 m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20.0 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The problem can be solved using the **equations of motion** under **constant acceleration**. Since the ball is dropped from rest, the **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**.
 
• The ball falls through a **vertical distance (s)** of **20 meters**. This represents the **displacement** of the object.
 
• The **acceleration (a)** acting on the ball is the **acceleration due to gravity (g)**, which is given as **10 m/s²**. *Hence, the values for u, s, and g are established.*
 
• The **third equation of motion** relates velocity, acceleration, and distance: **v² = u² + 2as**. Plugging in the known values, we get **v² = 0² + 2(10)(20)**.
 
• Calculating the product, **v² = 400**. Taking the **square root** of **400**, we find the **final velocity (v)** to be **20.0 m/s**. *Hence, the calculated velocity is 20.0 m/s.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• These equations were formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** and describe the relationship between **velocity**, **time**, **acceleration**, and **displacement** for an object moving with **uniform acceleration**.
 
• The three primary equations are: **v = u + at**, **s = ut + 1/2 at²**, and **v² = u² + 2as**.
 
• In this context, **v** is the **final velocity**, **u** is the **initial velocity**, **a** is the **acceleration**, **t** is the **time**, and **s** is the **displacement**.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity:**
 
 
• On **Earth**, the average value of **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, but for simplicity in competitive exams and school calculations, it is often taken as **10 m/s²**.
 
• The value of **g** varies slightly depending on the **location** (latitude and altitude) on the Earth's surface.
 
• This acceleration is always directed **downwards** towards the **center of the Earth**.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall Concept:**
 
 
• A **free-falling object** is an object that is falling under the **sole influence of gravity**.
 
• In a **vacuum**, all objects fall at the **same rate** regardless of their **mass**, as demonstrated by **Galileo Galilei**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Units and Dimensions:** The **SI unit** for **velocity** is **meters per second (m/s)**, and for **acceleration**, it is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**. It is essential to ensure units are consistent before applying formulas.
 
• **Sign Convention:** While solving physics problems, defining a **direction** as positive is crucial. If **downward motion** is considered positive, then both **acceleration (g)** and **displacement (s)** will be **positive**.
 
• **Mass Independence:** Note that the **mass** of the ball was not provided and is **not required** to calculate the final velocity in a free fall scenario, assuming **air resistance** is negligible.
 
• **Kinematics Applications:** These principles are used in various fields including **engineering**, **ballistics**, and **aerospace** to predict the motion of projectiles and falling bodies.
</ul

questions.question: Which part of Bryophyllum develops new plantlets for vegetative propagation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leaf margin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bryophyllum** (often called the air plant or miracle leaf) is a well-known example of a plant that undergoes **vegetative propagation** through its **leaves**.
 
• The **leaf margins** of **Bryophyllum** possess special **notches** where **adventitious buds** develop.
 
• These **buds** have the potential to grow into **new plantlets** while still attached to the parent leaf or after the leaf falls onto **moist soil**. ***Hence, the statement regarding leaf margins is correct.***
 
• Once these plantlets touch the **ground**, they develop their own **roots** and grow into independent plants, allowing the species to spread rapidly without the need for **seeds**.
 
• This process is a form of **asexual reproduction**, meaning the new plants are **genetically identical** to the parent plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• It is a type of **asexual reproduction** in which new plants are produced from **roots, stems, leaves, and buds**. Since reproduction is through the **vegetative parts** of the plant, it is known as vegetative propagation.
 
• Plants produced by this method take **less time** to grow and bear **flowers and fruits** earlier than those produced from **seeds**.
 
 
 
• **Propagation by Roots:**
 
 
• Certain plants like **Sweet potato** and **Dahlia** can give rise to new plants from their **modified roots**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect in the context of Bryophyllum.***
 
 
 
• **Propagation by Stem:**
 
 
• Many plants reproduce via **underground stems**. For example, **Potato** propagates through "eyes" (axillary buds on the **tuber**), and **Ginger** or **Turmeric** propagates through **rhizomes**.
 
• **Cacti** produce new plants when their **parts** (stems) get detached from the main plant body. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect for Bryophyllum.***
 
 
 
• **Propagation by Flowers:**
 
 
• **Flowers** are generally the **reproductive parts** of a plant involved in **sexual reproduction** (producing seeds), rather than vegetative propagation. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Natural Vegetative Propagules:** These are units of vegetative propagation such as **runners, rhizomes, suckers, tubers, offsets, and bulbs**.
 
• **Water Hyacinth:** Often called the **"Terror of Bengal,"** it propagates vegetatively at a phenomenal rate through **offsets** and can spread over a water body in a very short period.
 
• **Agave:** This plant utilizes **bulbils** (fleshy buds) for vegetative reproduction, which develop on the **floral axis**.
 
• **Significance:** This method is essential for plants that have lost the capacity to produce **viable seeds**, such as **banana, orange, rose, and jasmine**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the potential energy?

options.text: It cannot be converted into other forms of energy.
It is only present when an object is moving.
It depends on the object’s motion.
It is energy stored due to position or condition.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is energy stored due to position or condition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy** is defined as the **energy stored** in an object because of its **specific position**, **arrangement**, or **state**. Unlike kinetic energy, it does not require the object to be in motion to exist. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Potential energy can be **transformed** into various other forms of energy, such as **kinetic energy**, **thermal energy**, or **electrical energy**. For instance, water stored at a height in a dam has potential energy that converts into kinetic energy as it falls. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• It is not dependent on **motion**; rather, it is energy "at rest" or "stored." Kinetic energy is the form of energy that is strictly present only when an **object is moving**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The magnitude of potential energy depends on the **spatial configuration** (like height or distance) or **internal condition** (like tension in a spring) of the object, not its **velocity** or **speed**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Potential Energy:**
 
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy**: This is the energy an object possesses due to its **vertical position** or **height**. The formula used to calculate it is **PE = mgh**, where **m** is **mass**, **g** is **acceleration due to gravity** (approx **9.8 m/s²**), and **h** is **height**.
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy**: This is energy stored as a result of **deforming** an elastic object, such as **stretching a rubber band** or **compressing a spring**.
 
• **Chemical Potential Energy**: This energy is stored within the **chemical bonds** of a substance. Examples include the energy found in **food**, **batteries**, and **fuels** like **gasoline**.
 
 
 
• **SI Unit**: The **Standard International unit** for measuring potential energy is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: In physics, **work done** on an object to change its position or configuration is stored as **potential energy**. For example, lifting a **10 kg weight** to a height of **2 meters** requires work that remains in the object as stored energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation of Mechanical Energy**: In an **isolated system** without **friction** or **air resistance**, the sum of **Potential Energy** and **Kinetic Energy** remains **constant**. This is a fundamental principle in **classical mechanics**.
 
• **Reference Point**: Potential energy is always measured relative to a **zero-point** or **reference level**, such as the **ground** or **sea level**. If the height is zero at the reference point, the gravitational potential energy is also **zero**.
 
• **Real-world Applications**:
 
 
• **Hydropower**: Dams use the **gravitational potential energy** of water to spin **turbines**.
 
• **Archery**: A **drawn bow** stores **elastic potential energy** which is released to propel the **arrow**.
 
• **Construction**: A **pile driver** uses potential energy by lifting a **heavy weight** to a high position before dropping it.

questions.question: பூச்சிகளின் எந்த செயல்பாடு தாவரங்களில் ஊட்டச்சத்துக்களின் இழப்பை நேரடியாக ஏற்படுத்துகிறது?

The correct answer is __**செல் சாற்றை உறிஞ்சுதல்**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **செல் சாற்றை உறிஞ்சுதல்** என்பது பூச்சிகள் தாவரங்களின் தண்டுகள், இலைகள் அல்லது மொட்டுகளில் உள்ள திரவ ஊட்டச்சத்துக்களை நேரடியாக உறிஞ்சும் ஒரு செயல்பாடாகும். இதன் மூலம் தாவரத்தின் வளர்ச்சிக்குத் தேவையான **சர்க்கரை, அமினோ அமிலங்கள் மற்றும் நீர்** ஆகியவை பெருமளவில் குறைக்கப்படுகின்றன. ***எனவே, கூற்று 1 சரியானது.***
 
• **விழுந்த இலைகளை மட்டுமே உட்கொள்கிறது**: விழுந்த இலைகள் ஏற்கனவே சிதைவு நிலையில் உள்ளவை மற்றும் அவை தாவரத்தின் உயிருள்ள பாகங்களுடன் இணைக்கப்படவில்லை. எனவே, இவற்றை உட்கொள்வது தாவரத்தின் தற்போதைய ஊட்டச்சத்து நிலையை நேரடியாகப் பாதிப்பதில்லை. ***எனவே, கூற்று 2 தவறானது.***

• The sensation of sound persists in our brain for about **0.1 seconds**. This phenomenon is scientifically known as the **persistence of hearing**.
 
• To hear a **distinct echo**, the time interval between the original sound and the reflected sound must be at least **0.1 s**.
 
• If the reflected sound arrives at the ear in less than **0.1 seconds**, the human brain cannot distinguish it as a separate sound, and it instead blends with the original sound, often leading to **reverberation**.
 
• An **echo** is simply the repetition of sound caused by the **reflection of sound waves** from a hard surface such as a wall, mountain, or cliff.
 
• The minimum distance required to hear an echo depends on the **speed of sound** in the medium, which varies with **temperature** and **humidity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Calculation of Minimum Distance:**

• Using the time interval of **0.1 s** and speed of **344 m/s**, the total distance traveled by sound (to the obstacle and back) is **34.4 meters**.
 
• Therefore, the **minimum distance** between the source of sound and the obstacle must be half of that, which is **17.2 meters**.

• **Acoustic Materials:** To reduce unwanted echoes or reverberations in cinemas or concert halls, the ceilings and walls are usually covered with **sound-absorbent materials** like compressed fiberboard, rough plaster, or draperies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nature of Surface:** For an echo to be clear, the reflecting surface must be **large** relative to the **wavelength** of the sound and should be **rigid** enough to reflect rather than absorb the energy.
 
• **Multiple Echoes:** Successive reflections of sound can result in **multiple echoes**. A classic example is the rolling of **thunder**, which is caused by the successive reflections of sound from several reflecting surfaces like clouds and land.
 
• **Applications of Echo:** The principle of echo is utilized in technologies such as **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) to measure the depth of the sea or locate underwater objects, and in **medical ultrasound** imaging.
 
• **Effect of Temperature:** On a hotter day, the **speed of sound** is higher; therefore, the **minimum distance** required to hear an echo will also **increase** slightly compared to a cold day.

questions.question: A characteristic of a colloidal solution is that:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it is a heterogeneous mixture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **colloidal solution** is technically a **heterogeneous mixture** even though it often appears **homogeneous** to the naked eye. This is because the particles are not truly dissolved but are dispersed throughout the medium. ***Hence, the correct answer is it is a heterogeneous mixture.***
 
• The **particle size** in a colloid typically ranges from **1 nanometer to 1000 nanometers**. These particles are larger than those in a **true solution** but smaller than those in a **suspension**.
 
• One of the most distinct features of a colloid is the **Tyndall Effect**, which is the scattering of a beam of light by the **dispersed particles**, making the path of light visible.
 
• Colloidal particles do not settle down when left undisturbed for a long period, which indicates that the mixture is relatively **stable** compared to a suspension.
 
• While a colloid cannot be separated by **simple filtration** using ordinary filter paper, it can be separated using a process called **centrifugation** or by using specialized **ultrafilters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of a Colloid**:
 
 
• **Dispersed Phase**: This refers to the substance that is distributed in the form of colloidal particles (similar to a **solute**).
 
• **Dispersion Medium**: This is the continuous medium in which the particles are distributed (similar to a **solvent**).
 
 
 
• **Brownian Motion**: Colloidal particles exhibit a continuous, random, zig-zag motion known as **Brownian motion**. This kinetic energy helps prevent the particles from settling due to **gravity**.
 
• **Types of Colloids**:
 
 
• **Aerosol**: Solid or liquid dispersed in gas (e.g., **fog**, **smoke**, **clouds**).
 
• **Emulsion**: Liquid dispersed in liquid (e.g., **milk**, **butter**, **face cream**).
 
• **Sol**: Solid dispersed in liquid (e.g., **gold sol**, **muddy water**, **blood**).
 
• **Gel**: Liquid dispersed in solid (e.g., **jelly**, **cheese**, **boot polish**).
 
 
 
• **Ideal Solutions and Azeotropes**:
 
 
• An **Ideal Solution** is a **homogeneous mixture** that obeys **Raoult's Law** at all concentrations and temperatures.
 
• An **Azeotrope** is a liquid mixture that has a **constant boiling point** and the same composition in both the liquid and vapor phases during distillation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mixture Classification**: Mixtures are broadly classified into **homogeneous** and **heterogeneous**. A **true solution** (like **sugar in water**) is homogeneous, meaning its composition is uniform throughout. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **Colloid Stability**: The stability of a colloid is often maintained by **electrostatic forces**. Most colloidal particles carry a **charge** (either positive or negative), which causes them to repel each other and prevents aggregation.
 
• **Electrophoresis**: This is a technique used to demonstrate the presence of charges on colloidal particles by observing their movement toward **oppositely charged electrodes** under an **electric field**.
 
• **Dialysis**: This is a common purification method for colloids, used to remove **electrolytes** or **crystalloids** from a colloidal solution using a **semi-permeable membrane**.
</ul

questions.question: Inside the lungs, rapid exchange of gases takes place between the air and the blood. Which type of epithelial tissue helps in this process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Simple squamous epithelium**__.

__
 
• **Simple squamous epithelium** consists of a **single layer** of **thin, flattened cells** with irregular boundaries. These cells look like **scales** or **floor tiles** when viewed from above, which is why it is also known as **pavement epithelium**.
 
• In the **respiratory system**, this tissue forms the walls of the **alveoli** (tiny air sacs in the **lungs**). Its extreme thinness is a critical feature that facilitates the **rapid exchange of gases** through **diffusion**.
 
• The primary function of **simple squamous epithelium** is to provide a **semi-permeable membrane** for the passage of small molecules. This is essential for **oxygen** to move from the air into the **blood capillaries** and for **carbon dioxide** to move from the blood into the lungs to be exhaled. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Apart from the **lungs**, this tissue is also found lining the **blood vessels** (where it is specifically called **endothelium**), the **lymphatic vessels**, and the **heart**.
 
• The **nucleus** of these cells is typically **oval or spherical** and is located in the center of the cell, often creating a slight bulge due to the cell's overall thinness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stratified Squamous Epithelium**:
 
 
• Unlike simple epithelium, this consists of **multiple layers** of cells. Its main function is **protection** against mechanical and chemical **wear and tear**.
 
• It is found in the **skin (epidermis)**, **mouth**, **esophagus**, and **vagina**. The outermost layers may be **keratinized** (as in the skin) to prevent water loss and provide extra durability.
 
 
 
• **Ciliated Columnar Epithelium**:
 
 
• These are **tall, pillar-like cells** that possess **cilia** (fine hair-like protoplasmic outgrowths) on their free surface.
 
• They are found in the **respiratory tract** (bronchioles) and **fallopian tubes**. Their function is to move **particles or mucus** in a specific direction across the epithelial surface.
 
 
 
• **Cuboidal Epithelium**:
 
 
• As the name suggests, these cells are **cube-like** in shape. They are commonly found in the **ducts of glands** and **tubular parts of nephrons** in the **kidneys**.
 
• The main functions of **cuboidal epithelium** are **secretion** and **absorption**. In the **proximal convoluted tubule (PCT)** of the kidney, these cells often have **microvilli** to increase the surface area for absorption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Blood-Air Barrier**: The **diffusion membrane** in the lungs is composed of three layers: the thin **squamous epithelium** of alveoli, the **endothelium** of alveolar capillaries, and the **basement substance** between them. Its total thickness is much less than a **millimetre** (approx **0.5 micrometres**), optimizing **gas exchange**.
 
• **Epithelial Tissue Classification**: Animal tissues are classified into four main types: **Epithelial**, **Connective**, **Muscular**, and **Neural**. **Epithelium** is further divided based on **cell shape** (squamous, cuboidal, columnar) and **layering** (simple or stratified).
 
• **Cell Junctions**: Most epithelial cells are held together with little intercellular material by specialized **junctions** like **tight junctions** (prevent leaking), **adhering junctions** (cementing), and **gap junctions** (communication).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the homologous series?

options.text: Each successive member differs by -CH₂- group.
All members have different functional groups.
All members have the same molecular weight.
All members have the same boiling point.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Each successive member differs by -CH2- group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homologous series** is a sequence of **organic compounds** with the same **functional group** and similar **chemical properties** in which the members of the series can be represented by a **general formula**.
 
• Each successive member of a **homologous series** differs from the preceding one by a **-CH2-** unit (known as a **methylene group**). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Because each member differs by a **-CH2-** group, the **molecular mass** of each successive member increases by **14 units** (where **Carbon** is **12 u** and two **Hydrogen** atoms are **2 u**). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• All members of a **homologous series** possess the same **functional group**, which determines their **chemical reactivity** and **properties**. For instance, all **alkanes** contain only **single bonds**, while all **alcohols** contain the **-OH** group. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While **chemical properties** remain similar, **physical properties** like **boiling point**, **melting point**, and **solubility** show a regular **gradation** as the **molecular mass** increases. Generally, the **boiling point** increases with the addition of more **carbon atoms** due to stronger **intermolecular forces**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alkanes:**
 
 
• The **general formula** for **alkanes** is **CnH2n+2**.
 
• Examples include **Methane (CH4)**, **Ethane (C2H6)**, and **Propane (C3H8)**.
 
• In this series, **Ethane** differs from **Methane** by **-CH2-**, and **Propane** differs from **Ethane** by **-CH2-**.
 
 
 
• **Alkenes and Alkynes:**
 
 
• **Alkenes** follow the **general formula** **CnH2n** and contain at least one **double bond**.
 
• **Alkynes** follow the **general formula** **CnH2n-2** and contain at least one **triple bond**.
 
• Like alkanes, successive members of these series also differ by the **methylene group**.
 
 
 
• **Physical State Gradation:**
 
 
• As the **carbon chain length** increases in a **homologous series**, the **physical state** of the compounds often changes. For example, the first four **alkanes** (C1 to C4) are **gases** at **room temperature**, while those from C5 to C17 are **liquids**, and higher members are **solids**.
 
• The **density** of the compounds also tends to increase systematically with the **molecular weight**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Preparation:**
 
 
• All members of a **homologous series** can generally be prepared by similar **chemical methods** known as **general methods of preparation**.
 
• Their **chemical reactions** are largely identical because the **functional group** remains the same throughout the series.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The concept of **homologous series** was first proposed to simplify the study of **organic chemistry** by grouping millions of compounds into a few families.
 
• A **methylene unit (-CH2-)** has a **mass** of exactly **14.027 atomic mass units**.
 
• In **homologous series** involving **branched chains**, the **isomers** may show variations in **physical properties**, but the **general formula** and **functional group** rules still apply to the primary series.
 
• Common series include **Alcohols (CnH2n+1OH)**, **Carboxylic Acids (CnH2n+1COOH)**, and **Aldehydes (CnH2n+1CHO)**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a cyclic hydrocarbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclohexane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclohexane** is a **cyclic hydrocarbon** with the chemical formula **C6H12**. It consists of **six carbon atoms** arranged in a **ring structure**, with each carbon atom attached to **two hydrogen atoms**. ***Hence, the option Cyclohexane is correct.***
 
• **Methane** is the simplest **alkane** with the formula **CH4**. It is an **acyclic** (open-chain) hydrocarbon consisting of **one carbon atom** bonded to **four hydrogen atoms**. ***Hence, the option Methane is incorrect.***
 
• **Butane** is an **alkane** with the formula **C4H10**. It exists as a **straight-chain** or **branched-chain** molecule and does not form a ring. ***Hence, the option Butane is incorrect.***
 
• **Ethene** (also known as **ethylene**) is an **unsaturated hydrocarbon** with the formula **C2H4**. It contains a **carbon-carbon double bond** and is a **linear** (acyclic) molecule. ***Hence, the option Ethene is incorrect.***
 
• **Cyclic hydrocarbons** are organic compounds where the **carbon atoms** are linked to form one or more **closed rings**. These can be **saturated** (cycloalkanes) or **unsaturated** (cycloalkenes or aromatics).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• **Aliphatic Hydrocarbons:** These are **open-chain** compounds. They include **alkanes** (saturated), **alkenes** (double bond), and **alkynes** (triple bond).
 
• **Alicyclic Hydrocarbons:** These are **cyclic** but behave like **aliphatic** compounds. **Cyclohexane** and **cyclopentane** are primary examples.
 
• **Aromatic Hydrocarbons:** These contain at least one **benzene ring** (a six-carbon ring with alternating double bonds). **Benzene (C6H6)** is the most common **aromatic** compound.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Cyclohexane:**
 
 
• It is a **colorless, flammable liquid** with a distinctive **detergent-like odor**.
 
• It is primarily produced by the **hydrogenation** of **benzene** in the presence of a **nickel or platinum catalyst**.
 
• It is widely used as a **non-polar solvent** in the chemical industry and as an intermediate in the production of **nylon 6** and **nylon 6,6**.
 
 
 
• **General Formulas:**
 
 
• **Alkanes:** **CnH2n+2**
 
• **Alkenes:** **CnH2n**
 
• **Cycloalkanes:** **CnH2n** (Note that they have the same general formula as alkenes but different structures).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Methane (CH4):** It is a major component of **natural gas** and is a potent **greenhouse gas**. It is often referred to as **marsh gas**.
 
• **Butane (C4H10):** It is highly **flammable** and is commonly used as a **fuel** in **LPG** (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) cylinders and cigarette lighters.
 
• **Ethene (C2H4):** It is a **plant hormone** used commercially for the **artificial ripening of fruits** and in the production of **polyethylene** plastic.
 
• **Stability of Cyclohexane:** Unlike smaller rings like cyclopropane, **cyclohexane** is very stable because it can adopt **chair** and **boat conformations** to minimize **ring strain** and **torsional strain**. The **chair conformation** is the most stable form.
 
• **Historical Context:** **Cyclohexane** was first synthesized by **Marcellin Berthelot** in **1867** by reducing **benzene** with **hydroiodic acid** at high temperatures.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements about average velocity is NOT correct?

options.text: It depends on the direction of motion.
It is always the same as average speed.
It is the total displacement divided by total time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is always the same as average speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average velocity** is defined as the **total displacement** divided by the **total time** taken for the motion. Unlike speed, it accounts for the change in position from the starting point to the ending point in a specific direction. ***Hence, the statement that it is the total displacement divided by total time is correct.***
 
• Velocity is a **vector quantity**, which means it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**. Any change in the direction of motion, even if the speed remains constant, results in a change in velocity. ***Hence, the statement that it depends on the direction of motion is correct.***
 
• The **Standard International (SI) unit** for measuring both speed and velocity is **meters per second (m/s)**. Other units like **km/h** or **miles/hour** can be used, but **m/s** is the scientific standard. ***Hence, the statement that it is measured in m/s is correct.***
 
• **Average speed** is the total **distance** traveled divided by time, while average velocity is **displacement** divided by time. Since distance is a **scalar** and displacement is a **vector**, the magnitude of average velocity is only equal to average speed when an object moves in a **straight line** without changing its direction. In all other cases, such as circular or zigzag paths, average speed is greater than the magnitude of average velocity. ***Hence, the statement that it is always the same as average speed is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scalar vs. Vector:** **Speed** is a **scalar quantity** as it only describes how fast an object is moving (magnitude). **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** because it specifies the rate of change of position along with the **direction** of movement.
 
• **Distance vs. Displacement:** **Distance** is the actual length of the path covered by an object, regardless of direction. **Displacement** is the **shortest straight-line distance** between the **initial** and **final positions** of the object.
 
• **Zero Average Velocity:** A unique characteristic of average velocity is that it can be **zero** even if the object has been in motion. For example, if a runner completes one full lap on a **circular track** and returns to the **starting point**, the total displacement is **zero**, making the **average velocity 0 m/s**, whereas the average speed would be a positive value.
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional representation for average velocity is **[M⁰ L¹ T⁻¹]**, signifying that it is independent of mass but dependent on **length (L)** and **inverse time (T⁻¹)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mathematical Formula:** The formula for average velocity is expressed as **v_avg = Δx / Δt**, where **Δx** is the **change in position (displacement)** and **Δt** is the **time interval**.

questions.question: A botanist observes a plant exhibiting rapid growth at its shoot tip. Which type of plant tissue is most likely responsible for this growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Apical meristem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apical meristem** is a type of **meristematic tissue** located at the **growing tips of stems and roots** of plants.
 
• It is primarily responsible for the **increase in the length** of the plant, a process known as **primary growth**.
 
• The **shoot apical meristem (SAM)** is found at the **shoot tip** and gives rise to organs like **leaves and flowers** through rapid **cell division**. *Hence, the botanist's observation of growth at the shoot tip points to this tissue.*
 
• The **root apical meristem (RAM)** is located at the **root tip** and provides the cells necessary for the **root to extend** deeper into the soil.
 
• These tissues consist of **undifferentiated cells** that continue to divide throughout the **life of the plant**, ensuring constant **vertical expansion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lateral Meristem:**
 
 
• This tissue is found on the **lateral sides** of the **stems and roots**.
 
• It is responsible for **secondary growth**, which increases the **thickness or girth** of the plant.
 
• Common examples include the **vascular cambium** and **cork cambium**, which are vital for **woody plants**.
 
 
 
• **Intercalary Meristem:**
 
 
• This is located at the **base of leaves** or **internodes** (the regions between nodes).
 
• It is particularly prominent in **monocots** like **grasses**, allowing them to **regenerate** quickly after being eaten by **herbivores**.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Tissue:**
 
 
• These are cells that have **matured** and **lost the ability to divide**.
 
• They have a **fixed shape and size** and perform **specialized functions** like **protection, support, or conduction**.
 
• Examples include **parenchyma**, **xylem**, and **phloem**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cellular Characteristics:** Meristematic cells are characterized by **thin cellulose walls**, **dense cytoplasm**, and **large prominent nuclei**.
 
• **Absence of Vacuoles:** Unlike mature plant cells, **meristematic cells** usually **lack vacuoles** because they are in a state of continuous **metabolic activity** and division.
 
• **Differentiation:** The process by which **meristematic cells** take up a **permanent shape, size, and function** is called **differentiation**, leading to the formation of **permanent tissues**.
 
• **Discovery:** The term "**meristem**" was coined by **Karl Wilhelm von Nägeli** in **1858**, derived from the **Greek word 'meristos'**, meaning **divisible**.
